duplicate_and_wrapper_comparisons.reason: The limit-only theorem reads .2 of the L2-plus-limit producer under the same assumptions. This deliberate convenience wrapper is not a new primitive.
The identities read process fields by reflexivity. Continuous versus measurable locally bounded temperature require different constructor hypotheses. Fold field identities under constructors.

Both conclude terminal sphere Ito. The continuity API has stronger regularity premises; integrated rows derive generator integrability and omit those premises. Retain the current continuity API for its consumers and prefer the weaker integrated-row producer for measurable temperature. Count common assembly once conceptually; no direct compiled edge between these two is asserted.
Rows versus literal coordinate equations need actual construction. Continuous-temperature every-time derivative and measurable-temperature balance/AC/a.e. derivative must remain distinct.
Horizon-dependent centered residuals are weaker data than a global martingale. The adapter discharges integrability and centering.
Compact arbitrary-time grids, positive dyadic horizons, coordinate-energy sums and actual completed rows discharge mesh, finite-sum, representative and QV premises respectively.
Elementary, progressive, stopped, drift-perturbed, prefix, cross and weighted results differ. Approximation, compatibility, finite variation and polarization are real obligations.
One increment isometry, grid energy, grid-square stability and time-path-energy stability control different objects.
General bounded past multipliers require simple approximation and limit identification beyond the event case.
Exact scalar second moment, dyadic limit, mixed polarization and diffusion-row expansion differ in assumptions and conclusions. The dyadic limit is not a projection of the finite-grid result.
Definition, radial component, norm-square, derivative, derivative contraction, Hessian contraction, generator and extrinsic Laplacian are not the same interface.
Fallback selection, agreement on the set and measurability are different interfaces. The short identity has actual compiled consumers.
The Euclidean continuous bilinear statement reuses the algebraic basis theorem; do not count a new bilinear primitive.
